name: Data, Medicine & Law: The Legal Foundations of Digitalized Medicine
description: While state-of-the-art technologies such as AI systems and robotic procedures are being used in healthcare, in many areas it lags significantly behind the digital standard in other areas of life – for example, where fax machines are still used for data transmission. Based on the concept of a “data cycle,” the seminar examines the legal basis for the collection and storage of health data, the structure and regulation of data rooms, and access to this data in the context of data-driven and personalized medicine. The seminar focuses in particular on the requirements of data protection and IT security law as well as product safety law for software in the healthcare sector, the legal framework for data infrastructures, and access to health data for research and innovation. The seminar analyzes the interactions between technical developments and legal regulation and discusses the extent to which legal frameworks can promote, control, or inhibit innovation in the field of digitalized medicine.
